title: Boss: Typed Inventory
summary: Unions, narrowing, generics, utility types and exhaustive checks together.

steps.title: The job
steps.body: An inventory service receives untrusted JSON, validates it into typed records, and applies typed commands. Remember that only `tsc` checks the types: your functions must also behave correctly when given bad data at run time.

steps.title: Validate an item
prompt: interface Item { sku: string; qty: number; location: "shelf" | "backroom" }
type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; errors: string[] };
Collect **all** errors, in this order and with exactly these messages:
- not an object (or null): `["not an object"]` (stop there)
starter: interface Item { sku: string; qty: number; location: "shelf" | "backroom" }
type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; errors: string[] };
solution: interface Item { sku: string; qty: number; location: "shelf" | "backroom" }
type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; errors: string[] };
if (typeof raw !== "object" || raw === null) return { ok: false, errors: ["not an object"] };
const r = raw as Record<string, unknown>;
return { ok: true, value: { sku: r.sku as string, qty: r.qty as number, location: r.location as Item["location"] } };
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.eq("valid", { ok: true, value: { sku: "A1", qty: 3, location: "shelf" } }, parseItem({ sku: "A1", qty: 3, location: "shelf", extra: 1 }));
Dojo.eq("all errors", { ok: false, errors: ["sku", "qty", "location"] }, parseItem({ sku: "", qty: 1.5, location: "roof" }));
Dojo.eq("negative qty", { ok: false, errors: ["qty"] }, parseItem({ sku: "B", qty: -1, location: "backroom" }));
Dojo.eq("null", { ok: false, errors: ["not an object"] }, parseItem(null));
Dojo.eq("string", { ok: false, errors: ["not an object"] }, parseItem("x"));
hints: After the object check, `raw as Record<string, unknown>` lets you read properties as `unknown`.
Build only the known properties into `value`, so extras are dropped.

steps.title: Apply commands
prompt: Write `run(stock: Readonly<Record<string, number>>, cmd: Command): Record<string, number>` returning a **new** record:
- `receive` adds qty (a missing sku starts at 0)
- `ship` subtracts qty, but throws `Error("insufficient stock")` if it would go below 0
starter: function run(stock: Readonly<Record<string, number>>, cmd: Command): Record<string, number> {
solution: function run(stock: Readonly<Record<string, number>>, cmd: Command): Record<string, number> {
if (cmd.qty > have) throw new Error("insufficient stock");
template: {{CODE}}
const dojoS = Object.freeze({ A1: 5, B2: 1 });
Dojo.eq("receive existing", { A1: 8, B2: 1 }, run(dojoS, { kind: "receive", sku: "A1", qty: 3 }));
Dojo.eq("receive new", { A1: 5, B2: 1, C3: 2 }, run(dojoS, { kind: "receive", sku: "C3", qty: 2 }));
Dojo.eq("ship", { A1: 1, B2: 1 }, run(dojoS, { kind: "ship", sku: "A1", qty: 4 }));
Dojo.throws("ship too many throws", () => run(dojoS, { kind: "ship", sku: "B2", qty: 2 }));
Dojo.eq("count", { A1: 0, B2: 1 }, run(dojoS, { kind: "count", sku: "A1", qty: 0 }));
Dojo.eq("discontinue", { B2: 1 }, run(dojoS, { kind: "discontinue", sku: "A1" }));
Dojo.throws("unknown kind throws", () => run(dojoS, { kind: "teleport", sku: "A1" } as any));
hints: A computed key in a literal: `{ ...stock, [cmd.sku]: value }`.
Remove a key immutably with rest: `const { [cmd.sku]: _removed, ...rest } = stock;`

steps.title: Generic summary
prompt: Write `summarize<T>(items: readonly T[], keyOf: (item: T) => string, valueOf: (item: T) => number): Record<string, { count: number; total: number }>` grouping items by key and adding up their values.
// { shelf: { count: 2, total: 7 }, backroom: { count: 1, total: 10 } }
starter: function summarize<T>(items: readonly T[], keyOf: (item: T) => string, valueOf: (item: T) => number): Record<string, { count: number; total: number }> {
solution: function summarize<T>(items: readonly T[], keyOf: (item: T) => string, valueOf: (item: T) => number): Record<string, { count: number; total: number }> {
const out: Record<string, { count: number; total: number }> = {};
out[k] = { count: prev.count + 1, total: prev.total + valueOf(item) };
template: {{CODE}}
const dojoI = [
{ sku: "A", qty: 3, location: "shelf" },
{ sku: "B", qty: 10, location: "backroom" },
{ sku: "C", qty: 4, location: "shelf" },
Dojo.eq("by location", { shelf: { count: 2, total: 7 }, backroom: { count: 1, total: 10 } }, summarize(dojoI, i => i.location, i => i.qty));
Dojo.eq("by first letter of sku, counting 1 each", { A: { count: 1, total: 1 }, B: { count: 1, total: 1 }, C: { count: 1, total: 1 } }, summarize(dojoI, i => i.sku, () => 1));
Dojo.eq("empty", {}, summarize([], (x: string) => x, () => 1));
hints: `out[k] ?? { count: 0, total: 0 }` gives the running totals.
